title: Records bought in 1965 and 1986
summary: Wood bought records of John Casimir, Jim Robinson, Kid Howard, George Lewis and Kid Thomas, and finds Preservation Hall labels bewildering.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And then I did buy some records when I was down here in the summer of 65 to graduate, and I was kind of bewildered, because by that time, there were Preservation Hall record labels available, and there were a lot of records that I had never, I guess these recordings had been done, and I didn't have but so much money, and I didn't know which records to buy. But I did buy two that I, three, really, that I remember that I still cherish. One is a record that features John Casimir. It's got his picture on the cover.
Is that with his sit-down band or his brass band?
It's his brass band, I think. No, it's with the sit-down band.
Okay.
And it was done after he, I believe, you know, that the liner notes, whoever wrote them, were written after he died. When did he die? Do you know?
No, I haven't.
Early 60s sometime, probably.
Right in there. Yeah.
The other one,
I have a bad memory for dates and all that.

It was a record that features Jim Robinson, and I asked you about it, I think, and it's under the Pearl label, and you told me that that was his, named it that because it's his wife's name. That's right. Yeah.
It's the one that's got Kid Thomas and Ernie Cagnolite both on trumpet.
Yeah. They played it,
I Will Be Somewhere Working for the Lord.

Yeah, that's a good record, and I like that one. And then the other one that I have that I bought that same summer, is a Kid Howard record that was all hymns, and is recorded in the Zion Hill Baptist Church. And it starts off with a little welcome by the preacher, the minister of the church. I'm the Reverend Alexander Griffin, or whatever, and I want to welcome all these people. And that's, I enjoy that. But those, you know, I really, and last summer, again, is a bewildering array of records, and you don't know how to buy one. It's going to be any good. You can't listen to them ahead of time. And I bought several records. To my shame, I let them get warped in my car. It got too hot. But the one that I did buy, and I enjoyed a lot, but it's badly warped, is a George Lewis record of him playing hymns with just piano play and bass, I guess. A record you had something to do with.
Yeah. Well, that narrows it down. Yeah.

And, in fact, when my daughter was here earlier this week, we did go down to Preservation Hall one night, and there was one copy of that record still in the back bin, and I bought it to replace my warped one, and I bought them. That one, the Brunius one down there, too. And last time, I also bought the Kid Thomas record that has Sammy Remington on it, which Kid Thomas plays Red Wing. I bought it because I like that number, and I thought it's... Who is Sammy Remington? Yeah, he appears. I see his name on all these records that are down there. Is the name of him? And I don't know him at all.
Yeah, and he plays clarinet, usually. And he sounds a lot like George Lewis as a way of characterizing it.
And so he's helped with this recording. I mean, he's pushed recording a lot.
Yeah.
Well, it's pretty bewildering to confront all those records and not to know which one to buy and what have you.
